newsitem.title: USA: Equitable to make small acquisitions - CEO.
newsitem.headline: Equitable to make small acquisitions - CEO.

text.p: Equitable Resources Inc is likely to make a string of small acquisitions over the next year of companies that will provide energy management services, said Fred Abrew, Equitable's president and chief executive officer.

Moreover, he said his company is about to close a deal to acquire a Boston-based firm that will provide those types of services, although he declined to give details other than saying the small transaction is worth about $2 million.
"We're scurrying the countryside now to increase our acquisitions in this area," Abrew said in a brief telephone interview with Reuters. "We have a number of discussions going on."

Pittsburgh-based Equitable said earlier on Thursday that it launched a new subsidiary, ERI Services, to create and deliver energy solutions to businesses that are seeking to bolster energy efficiency while reducing costs.
Abrew said the acquisitions his company will make will be similar to ERI Services.

"What (those companies) do is re-engineer the way an organization uses energy to get the most efficient utilization," he said. "This will allow us to capture customers and drive down prices at the wellhead and generating station."
Abrew said buying energy management firms will help give Equitable leverage in a competitive, customer-driven deregulated utility industry.
"I think deregulation is coming a lot faster than perhaps the marketplace is prepared to understand," he said. "What we're trying to do is be a big energy service provider."
ERI Services, based in Pittsburgh, will account for five percent of Equitable's revenues at the end of the year. It's expected to account for nearly 25 percent by the year 2000.
Equitable Resources, a diversified energy supplier with $2 billion in assets, operates in 26 states.

Abrew said ERI Services will be able to tailor products to meet customers' energy needs and budget. Initially, the subsidiary will serve commercial customers, but will eventually serve residential customers, he said.
"I think by the end of 1997 we'll be prepared to start serving residential customers," he said.
ERI Services combines the expertise and customers of Equitable's previously announced acquisitions of Independent Energy Corp and Conogen Inc.
